If the refresh succeeds, later callers can use its replacement after validation. If nobody requests this key after 24 s, this request-triggered design starts no refresh.

Illustrative limits from the adapter, not measured latencies. The boxes show responsibilities, not a time scale. Connection setup and socket reads each have a 20 ms client limit; the 25 ms wrapper caps their combined GET wait. Event-loop cancellation is cooperative.

An illustrative schedule. The card moves from the source to App A, then towards the cache. Deletion tears away the token before the old card arrives. “Remember revision 2” includes a deliberately unsafe choice: after losing the remembered number, it treats missing as zero. P7 means product:v1:north:P7:en-GB:GBP.
Events in order, as text
states: App A proceeds without a revocable permission. The revision rule will compare source revisions when it fills.
App A reads revision 1. The card moves to App A, which pauses before publishing it.
App B commits revision 2. The authoritative source now says GBP 22.00; App A still holds GBP 20.00.
Deletion succeeds. The cache is empty, but App A can still write its old card.
No further change: the key remains empty while App A waits.
The unconditional write puts revision 1 back. Source and cache now disagree.

The bands add up to one cache lookup. Transit combines the outward and return trips for this accounting view. It does not mean the reply travels before execution. A miss would add source admission, a source read and possibly a fill after this lookup.

Traces as text
states: The client spends two milliseconds preparing the operation. Most of this trace’s delay lies ahead.
Communication accounts for 4 milliseconds. Connection setup, network delay and reply transfer belong to the client-visible path, outside the command execution timer.
Command execution takes twenty-two milliseconds. Correlate the request with server execution evidence before changing the cache deployment.
Decoding and validation take the final two milliseconds. The application can now return a valid hit. Keep the whole lookup inside the request deadline.

One possible order under asynchronous replication, drawn from Redis’s documented behaviour; no failover was executed for this figure. The elapsed time stays within the entry’s expiry. P7 abbreviates the north shop’s en-GB, GBP product-card key.

Failover as text
states: The source commits GBP 22.00 at revision 2. Neither cached copy has changed yet.
The primary applies DEL and replies successfully. Its replica has not received the deletion. The two cached states now differ.
The primary fails before the deletion reaches the replica. After promotion and client reconnection, the new endpoint still holds revision 1.
App A reads GBP 20.00 from the new primary. For a read requiring revision 2 or newer, this is an unusable hit. The source path still needs admission and remaining time.

Invented operating intervals, not a Redis simulation or measured throughput. Every interval contains 100 requests; a warm namespace answers 90% of its requests. The 30-start source allowance covers demand and warm-up together. The space units stand for measured groups of entries in a real rollout; they are not bytes or Redis allocation sizes.

Rollout as text
states: Two dots move to v2: ten requests. Its empty namespace misses on all ten. Add nine misses from v1: nineteen source reads, inside the thirty-start allowance.
The useful v2 entries now produce hits. Total demand work returns to ten reads. Check latency, errors and answer validity before increasing traffic.
Targeted warming prepares the answers the larger group will need. Five warm-up reads share this interval with ten demand reads. Both formats now occupy twelve space units.
The old readers have gone, but the rollback window remains open. Keep the old namespace’s invalidation and age rules working while it remains a possible destination.
The source commits revision 2. Invalidation reaches both formats. Controlled fills restore useful answers; this interval uses twenty source starts.
Traffic moves back to v1. Its format is old, but its product data has stayed current under the same freshness rules. The rollback can reuse its valid entries.
